statement: Definitions only, for the Track C proposal agent. No table number and no direction are given on purpose. Definitions are taken from docs/PHENOMENON_PROTOTYPES.md (P-STATE-1 as its v2 record); family surface terms are the approved_lexical terms of data/metadata/concept_map.yaml (approved_family_term excluded); place terms are drawn from the approved place-term set (oklahoma, stephens, california). F-FWI and F-HEAT are family-level pseudo-units. Historical periods are modeled baselines, never observations; the Fire Weather Index is a meteorological fire-danger index, never fire occurrence. Decision references are in data/manifest.json.

units.definition: The summer (June, July and August) Fire Weather Index, a meteorological fire-danger index and not fire occurrence, at the single ClimRR grid cell R106C361, comparing the modeled historical baseline 1995-2004 with the modeled end-century decade 2085-2094 under RCP8.5.

The summer (June, July and August) Fire Weather Index, a meteorological fire-danger index and not fire occurrence, over the ClimRR rows labelled State Oklahoma and NAME Stephens, comparing the modeled historical baseline 1995-2004 with the modeled end-century decade 2085-2094 under RCP8.5.
units.place_label: rows labelled State Oklahoma, NAME Stephens (reading the labels as a state and a county name is inferred_candidate)

units.definition: The number of summer days with daily maximum heat index above 105 °F, over the ClimRR rows labelled State California, comparing the modeled historical baseline 1995-2004 with the modeled end-century decade 2085-2094 under RCP8.5.
units.place_label: rows labelled State California (reading the label as a state name is inferred_candidate)

units.definition: The Fire Weather Index family as a whole, a meteorological fire-danger index and not fire occurrence, as projected in ClimRR for modeled historical and future periods; the exact metric, season and scenario are kept as provenance, not fixed here.
The heat index family as a whole, as projected in ClimRR for modeled historical and future periods; the exact metric, season and scenario are kept as provenance, not fixed here.
